questions.q: What is an API, in plain terms?
options: A defined way for one piece of software to ask another for data or an action, without either side needing to know the other's internals
A type of database used only for storing images
A programming language used to write web pages
A synonym for the internet itself
questions.explain: An API is a contract — the accepted requests and the shapes of the answers — that lets two programs interact without either needing to know how the other works inside.

questions.q: In an API call, what's the difference between the client and the server?
options: There is no real difference; the terms are interchangeable
The client only runs on mobile phones
The client sends the request; the server processes it and sends back the response
The server always asks the questions
questions.explain: The client is the program asking the question; the server is the program that does the work and answers it.

questions.q: What are the three moving parts of every API call, per this lesson?
options: Login, authenticate, logout
Request, process, response
Install, configure, deploy
Connect, disconnect, reconnect
questions.explain: The client sends a request, the server processes it, and the server sends back a response — the same three steps every time.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say learning APIs isn't just a prerequisite for AI engineering?
options: Because AI applications never actually use APIs
Because reading and shaping requests and responses to an AI provider's API is the real, ongoing work of building an AI application
Because APIs are only used for weather data
Because AI models run entirely inside the client with no server involved
questions.explain: When your app "calls Claude" or "calls GPT," it is sending a request to a server it doesn't control and reading back a response — exactly the pattern this lesson teaches.

questions.q: To ask a weather API for today's forecast, what do you actually need to know?
options: Nothing at all — it works automatically with no information
The internal source code of the weather service
The shape of the question it accepts, and the shape of the answer it gives back
The physical location of the weather service's servers
questions.explain: You don't need to know how the server works internally — only the agreed-upon contract: what requests it accepts and what responses it returns.
